issue.title: Update: Docker_Security_Cheat_Sheet / actually recommend to upgrade the container images
issue.body:
## What is missing or needs to be updated?

The Docker Chet Sheet asks to:

* upgrade the host;
* maintain provenance/SBOM info for the container images, etc.

but there is no explicit mention of actually managing the upgrades of the container images.

## How should this be resolved?

* Explicitly state that some upgrade process must be in place for the container images?
* Mention (timely) detection of vulns in container images?

i.e. generating a SBOM is not super useful if it is not exploited.

comments.body:
Thanks for raising this, @randomstuff. The cheat sheet covers host and engine updates, CI/CD image scanning and SBOM generation, but it does not explicitly require a process for rebuilding and updating container images or for keeping deployed images monitored for newly disclosed vulnerabilities. Adding that guidance would be a useful update. Would you like to work on a pull request for this?
